rows.name: title
rows.notes: The question. Required here for the reason it is required on the dialog — the surface takes its accessible name from this part — and an alert has a second one on top: the title is the question the two buttons answer, so a nameless alert is an unanswerable one. Narrowed the same way, so `null`, `undefined` and `false` cannot reach it either.

rows.name: description
rows.notes: The consequence, and required on an alert where it is optional on a dialog. The APG asks an `alertdialog` to point `aria-describedby` at the message that explains the alert, and the machine only wires that once the part is placed — so an alert without a description is one that announces its question and never its stakes. The comment here always said the title alone rarely can; the type says it now.
